conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: MODULE-NAME Function, (Which type of dynamic length elementary item is used as the returned value)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §15.65.4 r1 (cite.py OK §15.65.4 1)) requires the type to be documented when more than one type of dynamic-length elementary item is supported; §8.5.1.10.2 (cite.py --find) makes the structure either implementor-defined or named by a DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE clause, and COBOL.NET supports both plus both classes (D-DL3, DOC-A.1-62), so the condition holds. Code: IntrinsicCatalog.cs:328 registers MODULE-NAME with IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric; CobolModule.Name(int) returns a System.String (the carrier of a structure-less DYNAMIC LENGTH item). Probe probe/mn.cob --std 2023: [MNPROG] LENGTH 6; ACTIVATING in main [ ] LENGTH 1; MOVE MODULE-NAME(STACK) to a PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH item -> [MNPROG; ] length 8; --std 2014 -> COBOLNET1502. No golden or unit test pins the type (ModuleStackInvariantTests pins item 133's no-trailing-spaces), so Pinned by is honestly empty. Incidental: BYTE-LENGTH(FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(CURRENT)) is refused with a COBOLNET1627 message calling the argument a numeric literal - already owned by kb/Work PB1068. Previously the substance sat only in DOC-A.1-133's cell.
rows.rule-text: MODULE-NAME Function, (Which type of dynamic length elementary item is used as the returned value). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon the implementor supporting more than one type of dynamic length elementary item. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.65, MODULE-NAME function, Returned value, rule 1)

rows.subject: MULTIPLY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR2 'Identifier-3 shall reference a data item of category numeric or numeric-edited.' (cite --check 14.9.26.3 OK). Probes: GIVING PIC X -> COBOLNET1675 (N4); GIVING group -> 1675 (N13); GIVING national -> 1675 (N18); GIVING ZZ9.99- accepted and stores 8.25 (p1). No spec-derived golden/negative -> test-needed. [code-location note: (Receivers editedOk:true '§14.9.26.3 SR2')] || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (MULTIPLY formats 1 and 2 with the SIZE ERROR / NOT SIZE ERROR pair; the rounded-phrase MODE option carries 14.7.4's own edition)
rows.rule-text: Identifier-3 shall reference a data item of category numeric or numeric-edited.

rows.subject: MULTIPLY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR3 'Literal-1 and literal-2 shall be numeric literals.' (cite --check 14.9.26.3 OK). Probes: literal-1 "12" -> COBOLNET0844 (N5); literal-2 "12" in F2 -> 0844 (N6); SPACE -> 0844 (N14); ZERO accepted (N15) per 8.3.3.6.3 SR1a (ZERO permitted where a numeric literal is required). No negative golden -> test-needed. [code-location note: (COBOLNET0844)] || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (MULTIPLY formats 1 and 2 with the SIZE ERROR / NOT SIZE ERROR pair; the rounded-phrase MODE option carries 14.7.4's own edition)
rows.rule-text: Literal-1 and literal-2 shall be numeric literals.

rows.subject: MULTIPLY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR4 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the composite of operands ... is determined by using all of the operands in the statement.' (cite --check 14.9.26.3 OK). Unlike ADD/SUBTRACT GIVING (which exclude receivers per their SR1b), MULTIPLY passes the GIVING receivers into the composite. Probe CP.cob: 9(5) x 9(5) GIVING 9(20)V9(11) = 31 accepted; MULTIPLY V9(12) BY 9(20) -> COBOLNET0805 (32); MULTIPLY 0.000000000001 BY B GIVING 9(20) -> 0805 (32, GIVING counted); not applied under STANDARD-DECIMAL (SD.cob). Note (14.7.7's subject, not this row): the cap is 31 at every edition, including --std 85, a documented reading in CheckComposite. No MULTIPLY composite negative golden (l1-add-composite-over-31 is ADD) -> test-needed. [code-location note: (CheckComposite('MULTIPLY',[a,b],recv) / ([a],byRecv))] || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (native arithmetic as a named mode; the composite cap itself is 14.7.7's)
rows.rule-text: When native arithmetic is in effect, the composite of operands described in 14.7.7, Arithmetic statements, is determined by using all of the operands in the statement.

rows.subject: MULTIPLY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR3: 'When format 1 or 2 is used and standard-decimal, or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the product equals the result of the arithmetic expression' (cite --check 14.9.26.4 OK). Probe SD.cob (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL): MULTIPLY A(123456789012345678.123456789) BY B(987654321.987654321) GIVING R(S9(27)V9(4)) ROUNDED -> ...800.4569 = exact product rounded (python Decimal); MULTIPLY 1.1 BY K(1.25) -> 1.37 (truncated). The native composite cap is correctly not applied under standard-decimal (CheckComposite returns early). The STANDARD-BINARY half is declined (COBOLNET0806) under docs/CONFORMANCE.md row 2 'Not claimed - REVISITABLE' (PB198), carried by the derived verdict standard-binary-only; no owner decision needed here. No spec-derived golden exercises MULTIPLY under STANDARD-DECIMAL -> test-needed. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the modes the rule names are those of the ARITHMETIC clause, 11.9.5; standard-decimal/standard-binary as named by this 2023 text)
rows.rule-text: When format 1 or 2 is used and standard-decimal, or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the product equals the result of the arithmetic expression (multiplier \* multiplicand) where the values for multiplier and multiplicand are as defined in General rules 1 and 2 for the respective formats.

rows.subject: NULL object reference
rows.adjudicator-notes: "NULL shall not be specified as a receiving operand." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.3 -> OK, SR1). At 2002 and later NULL is a reserved token, not a cobolWord, so it cannot head a dataReference in any receiving slot. SetFormatSelection.KindOf's comment records that SR1 is enforced by the grammar. Probed at 2023, and at 2002 for SET: `SET NULL TO G`, `SET NULL G TO NULL`, `MOVE G TO NULL`, `INVOKE CN1 "NEW" RETURNING NULL` and `INITIALIZE NULL` are all refused with COBOLNET0901. A bare `USING NULL` bound BY REFERENCE (the formal's mode) is refused COBOLNET0828, which §14.9.23.3 SR9 also requires. Every receiving position is refused. The diagnostic cites §8.9 (reserved word) rather than this SR, which is a message-quality point, not a missed rejection. At 1985 NULL is an ordinary user word and the rule does not apply. No spec-derived negative test covers this SR by name. Probe files: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null-object-reference/n1,n2,n3,n6,n7.cob
rows.rule-text: NULL shall not be specified as a receiving operand.

rows.subject: National literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.3 "Two contiguous quotation symbol characters matching the quotation symbol used in the opening delimiter" -> OK (rule 3). STR_BODY lexes '""' inside a quote-delimited body and '\'\'' inside an apostrophe-delimited one; Decode collapses the doubled OPENING delimiter only. Probe p1: N"A""B" -> A"B (LENGTH 3), N'A''B' LENGTH 3, VALUE N'a''b' -> a'b, and the non-matching quote N'A"B' is ordinary content (LENGTH 3). Second sentence (same coded character set representation as the opening quote): only the basic quotation mark/apostrophe are delimiters, so a doubled pair is necessarily in the opening delimiter's representation; a full-width quote is plain content. No spec-derived test pins the doubled delimiter inside N".." - test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]
rows.rule-text: Two contiguous quotation symbol characters matching the quotation symbol used in the opening delimiter represent a single occurrence of that quotation symbol character in the content of the literal. The two contiguous quotation symbol characters shall be in the same coded character set representation as the opening quotation symbol.

rows.subject: National literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: "National literals are of the class and category national" (cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 -> OK, rule 2). ClassOf maps both prefixes N and NX to LiteralClass.National, NationalLiteralOperand binds Category = PicCategory.National, ConcatOperand keeps National. Probe e1 (--std 2002/2014): MOVE N"AB" TO PIC X and MOVE NX"0041" TO PIC X both refused COBOLNET0819 (national sender to alphanumeric receiver, Table 16) - the category is observed for both formats. No test found that asserts class/category for BOTH formats from this rule (NationalLiteral_InNumericContext_Rejects0844 pins only the not-numeric half of F1), so test-ref left empty. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]
rows.rule-text: National literals are of the class and category national.

rows.subject: Numeric literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: "A literal shall contain at least one digit." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 1)). Enforced by construction in the lexer: INT_BODY is [0-9]+, DEC_BODY is [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+, SIGNED_*LIT are [+-] followed by those bodies, and numericLiteralCore's comma alternatives (INTEGERLIT COMMA INTEGERLIT | COMMA INTEGERLIT) each carry an INTEGERLIT. No token or parser alternative forms a numeric literal from a bare sign or a bare decimal point, so a digitless 'literal' can only be a parse error. Structural rule; no probe needed beyond confirming the fragments. No dedicated negative golden -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the formation/value rules are unchanged across editions; only the digit ceiling moves: 18 at COBOL-85, 1 through 31 from 2002 per the clause's lead paragraph)]
rows.rule-text: A literal shall contain at least one digit.

rows.subject: OBJECT paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR1 "Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition" (cite.py --check 11.8.3 OK). CaptureImplements resolves each name through the §8.4.6.4 funnel with Want.Interface at the class's scope (cite.py --check 8.4.6.4 OK); a REPOSITORY in the OBJECT paragraph itself is forbidden by §12.3.3 SR3 so the class scope is the only one. Probes (probe dir out/probe/object-paragraph (gen.py)): p3 interface defined in the group and declared only in a PROGRAM's REPOSITORY -> COBOLNET0840 ('not declared in the REPOSITORY paragraph'); p4 declared as `CLASS IA` -> 0840; p5 IMPLEMENTS names a class -> 0840; positive p1/p8 compile. test-ref empty: unit:OoClassTablePositionTests' IMPLEMENTS NOIF2 case pins an interface that IS declared in the REPOSITORY but defined nowhere (an external-repository question, not an SR1 violation), and no golden pins the defined-but-undeclared refusal - test-needed (negative: p3 shape). Side note: the message for an undefined interface reads 'no such an interface' (OoNameResolution.Resolve kind string) - cosmetic. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO facility, introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; absent from X3.23-1985) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Oo/OoClassTable.cs#Build (CaptureImplements); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Oo/OoNameResolution.cs#Resolve; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Oo/OoNameResolution.cs#Lookup
rows.rule-text: Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition.

rows.subject: OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR10 (cite.py --check 12.3.6.4 "the initial program collating sequences are the native alphanumeric collating sequence and the native national collating sequence" -> OK §12.3.6.4 10)). No PCS clause leaves DataBinder.Collating / NationalCollating null (the native fast path; no __COLLATE / __COLLATE_NAT member is emitted); a contained unit copies the container's pair in InheritConfiguration, so the 'not contained within a source unit for which a PCS is specified' condition is honoured (pb60_nested_configuration_inheritance pins the inherited arm). Probe gr10.cob (no PCS anywhere, outer + nested program): "a" > "B" and N"a" > N"B" both TRUE (native code order) in outer and contained program; ORD("A")=66, ORD(N"B")=67. pb373 asserts the default (GR10) alphanumeric arm by relation/ORD; the national native arm is pinned by conformance:2002/l1_char_national_argument_bound (65 536 native national positions). || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty: conformance:2023/pb373_object_computer_name_inert does not pin GR10) — The code conforms: with no PCS anywhere both sequences stay null (native code order) and emit no __COLLATE members. My probe added a sibling-pollution attack: a separate program with PCS REV in the same compilation group does not leak into the PCS-less outer program or its contained program; relation, MAX and table SORT stay native, and national stays native. BUT the cited test does not pin this rule. pb373 runs all four legs under GR10 and compares their signatures to EACH OTHER. Its header says 'No implementor-defined VALUE is pinned - only that all four legs agree'. A non-native default applied uniformly would still pass. So it pins GR2-GR4 invariance, not GR10's native sequence. The rule is CONFORMS-but-untested. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the national half from 2002)]
rows.rule-text: When the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is not specified and the source unit is not contained within a source unit for which a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is specified, the initial program collating sequences are the native alphanumeric collating sequence and the native national collating sequence.
